_comment: JSON Merge Patch (RFC 7396) applied to floatplane-openapi-specification.json before code generation. Use this to (a) loosen 'required' fields where the community spec is too strict for real responses, (b) add fields the community spec is missing, and (c) document spec gaps in one place that both iOS and Android pick up. The merger lives at packages/openapi/scripts/apply-overlay.py and is called from generate-swift.sh and generate-kotlin.sh. floatcli/spec.py also applies it at runtime so its validation matches the iOS/Android codegen.

PostMetadataModel._comment: Real responses occasionally omit isFeatured on certain post types (livestream VODs in particular). Treating it as optional keeps the home feed decoder from blowing up on a single non-conforming post. See HomeFeedViewModel + LossyArray for the wider safety net. Also adds displayDuration: real responses return this on every post (observed on /api/v3/content/post and /creator/list). On a multi-video post like C3GeAE0LmM (videoCount=3), videoDuration is the SUM of all videos (1457s) while displayDuration is the primary video's duration (1365s). Cards should prefer displayDuration so they don't show a misleading total when posts contain multiple parts (see GH #29).

displayDuration.description: Duration in seconds of the primary video on a post, distinct from videoDuration (which sums every video attachment). Use this on cards/feeds for multi-video posts.

BlogPostModelV3._comment: As of 2026-10-03 Floatplane's list/feed endpoints (/content/creator, /content/creator/list, /content/related) return a slimmed-down post: no attachmentOrder, wasReleasedSilently or *Attachments arrays (use /content/post?id= for those), a creator without owner/subscriptionPlans/discoverable/subscriberCountDisplay/incomeDisplay/liveStream/cover/card, and a channel without creator/cover/card. With the upstream-required lists every feed post failed to decode and the home screen went blank. Verified against 45 live posts. Clients must fetch /content/post for video attachment ids before playback.

textMarkdown.description: Markdown rendering of `text`. Present on live responses, absent from the upstream spec.

ChannelModel._comment: The channel embedded in feed posts (BlogPostModelV3.channel) is now just {id, title, urlname, about, icon}: no creator, cover or card. See BlogPostModelV3 above.

SubscriptionPlanModel._comment: Real /api/v3/content/creator/list responses omit `interval` on every subscriptionPlan we've observed (e.g. LTT). The upstream spec marks it required, which would crash decode for any post whose creator has plans without it (= every post). Loosened here; see fixture get_api_v3_content_creator_list_ids_0_*.json captured 2026-05-08.

UserModel._comment: Real responses include a `badges: [string]` array on the user object that the upstream spec doesn't model. The spec also marks UserModel additionalProperties: false, which causes strict validators to reject the badges field. Observed in /api/v3/comment, /api/v3/comment/replies, and anywhere a CommentModel.user is rendered. Removing additionalProperties allows the field through; adding it explicitly lets future codegen emit a typed accessor.

badges.description: Badge IDs awarded to the user. Not in the upstream spec; observed in production on comment authors.

CreatorModelV3._comment: The inline owner schema on CreatorModelV3 mirrors the badges-on-user pattern: `additionalProperties: false` plus no `badges` field. Real responses on /api/v3/creator/info, /creator/named, and /creator/list all carry badges on owner.

badges.description: Badge IDs awarded to the owning user. Not in the upstream spec.

ImageModel._comment: Real responses omit `childImages` entirely on placeholder/data-URI icons (e.g. small base64 PNGs returned for users without uploaded avatars, observed in /api/v3/content/history). The upstream spec marks it required + nullable, but the field can be absent. Both iOS Codable (decodeIfPresent for optional vars) and Moshi-Kotlin (nullable fields default to null) already handle the missing case — only the spec is too strict.

ContentPostV3Response._comment: selfUserInteraction is returned by /api/v3/content/post but absent from the upstream spec. The field is a single interaction string (or null) when present on the post detail response — NOT an array. Observed values: 'like' (user liked the post), 'dislike' (user disliked), null (no interaction). See fixture get_api_v3_content_post_id_C3GeAE0LmM.json captured 2026-05-19 where selfUserInteraction="like". iOS wraps this in BlogPostDetailedWithInteraction (Models/ContentModels.swift) to decode a single enum.

selfUserInteraction.description: The interaction the current user has performed on this post. Null when no interaction. Not in the upstream spec; observed in production.

CommentModel._comment: Upstream types userInteraction as UserInteractionModel (array | null) — that matches /api/v3/content/post responses but NOT /api/v3/comment responses, where the field comes back as a single string ("like" / "dislike") or null. Confirmed in a live response captured 2026-05-19. Decode the comment shape with a single-value type so the comments list stops failing the moment a user has actually liked a comment. The explicit `$ref: null` is RFC 7396 for "remove the upstream $ref so our inline definition wins".

CommentV3ReplyRequest._comment: Reply-to-comment request body, restored after live API testing confirmed POST /api/v3/comment rejects any field other than {blogPost, text}. Real reply path is POST /api/v3/comment/reply with {blogPost, text, replyTo}. This matches the pre-regen codegen the Android app was originally built against (see commit d021803).

blogPost.description: The GUID of the blogPost the parent comment is on.

text.description: The text of the reply being posted.

replyTo.description: The GUID of the parent CommentModel being replied to.

WatchHistoryEntry.description: One entry in /api/v3/content/history. Records that a user watched a piece of content along with their last-known progress. Not in the upstream spec.

WatchHistoryBlogPost.description: Variant of BlogPostModelV3 returned inside watch-history entries. Differs from the home-feed shape in that videoAttachments / audioAttachments / pictureAttachments / galleryAttachments are arrays of string IDs rather than full attachment objects.

/api/v3/content/creator/list._comment: Upstream spec switched the `fetchAfter` query param from a free-form bracket-encoded object to a typed array (items: ContentCreatorListLastItems). The new shape makes openapi-kotlin-generator emit a Retrofit @Query with List<T>, which does NOT serialize as the bracket-form fetchAfter[0][creatorId]=… that Floatplane requires (see the example URL the upstream description still cites). Reverting the param to an object schema makes codegen emit a @QueryMap, matching HomeFeedViewModel's manual key encoding. Re-evaluate when upstream fixes the param style.

parameters.name: ids
parameters.description: The IDs of the creators to retrieve blog posts from.

parameters.name: fetchAfter
parameters.description: For pagination. Floatplane expects bracket-encoded keys like `fetchAfter[0][creatorId]=…&fetchAfter[0][blogPostId]=…&fetchAfter[0][moreFetchable]=…`. Codegen emits a @QueryMap; the caller serializes the cursors by hand. See HomeFeedViewModel.

/api/v3/content/history._comment: Endpoint exists in production but is missing from the upstream spec. Returns the most recently-watched posts (paged via offset). The blogPost embedded in each entry has a different shape from BlogPostModelV3: video/audio/picture/galleryAttachments are arrays of string IDs rather than full objects. iOS hand-models this as WatchHistoryBlogPost.

get.description: Returns the authenticated user's watch history, paginated by offset.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: How many entries to skip (for pagination).

/api/v3/content/progress._comment: Upstream types the 200 response as text/plain string "OK" (literal, no JSON quotes). Retrofit + Moshi parses the body, finds non-JSON text, and throws JsonEncodingException 'malformed JSON at path $' — every time progress saves. Setting content to null per RFC 7396 strips the response schema so codegen emits Response<Unit>; we never read the body anyway.

/api/v3/comment/reply._comment: Reply-to-comment endpoint, observed in production. POST /api/v3/comment rejects any extra field beyond {blogPost, text} with 400 "X is not allowed", confirming replies use a separate path. Brought back from the pre-regen Android codegen (commit d021803).

post.description: Post a reply to an existing comment. Distinct from the top-level POST /api/v3/comment endpoint, which doesn't accept a parent-comment reference.
